'''Johnjoe McFadden''' (born 17 May 1956) is an Anglo-Irish scientist, academic and writer. He is Professor of Molecular Genetics at the [[University of Surrey]], United Kingdom.

==Life==
McFadden was born in Donegal, Ireland but raised in the [[United Kingdom|UK]]. He holds joint [[British nationality law and the Republic of Ireland#Access to British citizenship for Irish citizens|British and Irish Nationality]]. He obtained his BSc in Biochemistry [[University of London]] in 1977 and his PhD at [[Imperial College London]] in 1982. He went on to work on [[Genetic disorder|human genetic diseases]] and then [[infectious diseases]], at [[St Mary's Hospital, London|St Mary's Hospital Medical School]], London (1982–84) and [[St George's Hospital Medical School]], London (1984–88) and then at the [[University of Surrey]] in [[Guildford]], UK.

For more than a decade, McFadden has researched the [[genetics]] of [[microbes]] such as the agents of [[tuberculosis]] and [[meningitis]] and invented a test for the diagnosis of meningitis. He has published more than 100 articles in scientific journals on subjects as wide-ranging as bacterial genetics, tuberculosis, [[idiopathic]] diseases and [[Artificial life|computer modelling of evolution]]. He has contributed to more than a dozen books and has edited a book on the genetics of [[mycobacteria]]. He produced a widely reported artificial life computer model which modelled evolution in organisms.

McFadden has lectured extensively in the UK, Europe, the US and Japan and his work has been featured on radio, television and national newspaper articles particularly for the ''[[The Guardian|Guardian]]''. His present post, which he has held since 2001, is Professor of Molecular Genetics at the University of Surrey. Living in London, he is married and has one son.

==Quantum evolution==

McFadden wrote the popular science book, ''Quantum Evolution''.<ref name="McFadden">{{cite book | last=McFadden | first=J. | year=2000 | url=http://www.surrey.ac.uk/qe/quantumevolution.htm | title=Quantum Evolution | publisher=[[HarperCollins]] | isbn=978-0-00-255948-5 | access-date=22 October 2005 | archive-date=23 June 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160623041743/http://www.surrey.ac.uk/qe/quantumevolution.htm | url-status=dead }}</ref> The book examines the role of [[quantum mechanics]] in life, [[evolution]] and [[consciousness]]. The book has been described as offering an alternative evolutionary mechanism, beyond the [[Modern synthesis (20th century)|neo-Darwinian]] framework.<ref>Gunter, Pete. A. Y. (2006). ''Darwinism: Six Scientific Alternatives''. ''The Pluralist'' 1 (1): 13-30.</ref>

The book received positive reviews by ''[[Kirkus Reviews]]'' and ''[[Publishers Weekly]]''.<ref>[https://www.kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/johnjoe-mcfadden/quantum-evolution/ "Quantum Evolution: The New Science of Life"]. ''[[Kirkus Reviews]]''.</ref><ref>[https://www.publishersweekly.com/978-0-393-05041-7 "Quantum Evolution: The New Science of Life"]. ''[[Publishers Weekly]]''.</ref> It was negatively reviewed in the journal ''[[Heredity (journal)|Heredity]]'' by evolutionary biologist [[Wallace Arthur]].<ref>Arthur, Wallace. (2000). [https://www.nature.com/articles/6887651 ''Quantum Evolution: The New Science of Life'']. ''[[Heredity (journal)|Heredity]]'' 85: 99.</ref>

==Writing==

In 2006 McFadden co-edited the book, ''Human Nature: Fact and Fiction'' on the insights of both science and literature on human nature, with contributions from [[Ian McEwan]], [[Philip Pullman]], [[Steven Pinker]], [[A.C. Grayling]] and others. 
<ref>{{cite book|last1=Headlam Wells|first1=Robin|last2=McFadden|first2=Johnjoe|title=Human Nature: Fact and Fiction|date=2006|publisher=Bloomsbury|location=London|isbn=9780826485465|url=http://www.bloomsbury.com/uk/human-nature-fact-and-fiction-9780826485465/}}</ref>

in 2014 McFadden co-wrote the popular science book, ''Life on the Edge: The Coming Age of Quantum Biology'', in which he and [[Jim Al-Khalili]] further explore quantum biology and particularly recent findings in photosynthesis, enzyme catalysis, avian navigation, olfaction, mutation and neurobiology.
<ref>{{cite book|last1=Al-Khalili|first1=Jim|last2=McFadden|first2=Johnjoe|title=Life on the Edge: The Coming Age of Quantum Biology|orig-year=2014 |year=2015 |publisher=Bantam Press|location=London|isbn=978-0593069318}}</ref>
The book received positive reviews, for example:

:"'Life on the Edge’ gives the clearest account I’ve ever read of the possible ways in which the very small events of the quantum world can affect the world of middle-sized living creatures like us. With great vividness and clarity it shows how our world is tinged, even saturated, with the weirdness of the quantum." (Philip Pullman)

:"Hugely ambitious ... the skill of the writing provides the uplift to keep us aloft as we fly through the strange and spectacular terra incognita of genuinely new science." (Tom Whipple The Times)

McFadden regularly writes articles for ''[[The Guardian]]'' newspaper<ref>{{cite web|last1=McFadden|first1=Johnjoe|title=Articles|website=[[TheGuardian.com]] |url=https://www.theguardian.com/profile/johnjoemcfadden}}</ref> on topics as varied as quantum mechanics, evolution and [[Genetically modified food|genetically modified crops]], and has reviewed books there. [[The Washington Post]] and [[Frankfurter Allgemeine Sonntagszeitung]] have also published his articles.

* Life Is Simple: How Occam’s Razor Set Science Free and Unlocked the Universe (Basic Books, 384pp) ISBN 9781529364934
